selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: In the passage, what is spring presented as a sign or example of?
questions.answer: It is presented as a worldly example of the gathering after resurrection and of being brought back to life.

questions.question: About how many examples of reviving the dead are said to appear in spring, and over what time period?
questions.answer: Around three hundred thousand examples appear within a few weeks.

questions.question: What four forms of renewal are mentioned in connection with a tree?
questions.answer: The tree itself, its leaves, its blossoms, and its fruits.

questions.question: After spring is shown again in a way that matches the earlier one, what kinds of things are given to each species?
questions.answer: Each species receives its food, means of protection, distinguishing outward form, duties and release from duties, and whatever equipment it needs.

questions.question: How are these gifts and arrangements carried out? Give two or three features named in the passage.
questions.answer: They are carried out with precision and order, at the right time, and without mistake, neglect, or confusion.

questions.question: Why does the passage treat this springtime ordering like an army?
questions.answer: Because many different species are managed together in a disciplined and organized way, as if they were many groups within one great force.

questions.question: What qualities of Allah are said to be shown through this yearly renewal?
questions.answer: His unity, His absolute oneness, His uniqueness, His limitless power, and His endless mercy.

questions.question: Besides power and mercy, what other aspects of divine rule are said to appear here?
questions.answer: Perfect lordship, sovereignty, and wisdom.

questions.question: What does the image of writing on the face of the earth suggest about spring?
questions.answer: It suggests that spring openly displays a clear message of divine unity across the earth for anyone willing to notice it.

questions.question: What is the main point of the whole passage?
questions.answer: The careful revival and provision seen every spring serves as strong evidence that one all-powerful and merciful Lord governs all things.

questions.question: What central event in spring is used as evidence in this passage?
questions.answer: The repeated bringing to life of countless living kinds after a period that resembles death.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention “a few weeks” instead of a long span of time?
questions.answer: To stress how quickly and easily this vast renewal takes place.

questions.question: In what way does the example of the tree strengthen the argument?
questions.answer: It shows resurrection-like renewal not only in one broad sense, but in several layers within a single living thing.

questions.question: What does the passage imply by saying spring is shown again like the one before it?
questions.answer: It implies continuity, consistency, and deliberate control rather than random change.

questions.question: What is meant by each species receiving suitable provision and equipment?
questions.answer: Each kind is given what fits its own nature and needs, not a careless or one-size-fits-all share.

questions.question: Which is emphasized more in the passage: disorderly abundance or measured care?
questions.answer: Measured care is emphasized.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the statement that things arrive unexpectedly yet on time?
questions.answer: Their arrival does not come from the creatures’ own planning, but from a higher will that provides exactly when needed.

questions.question: How does the passage connect spring to belief in one Creator rather than many powers?
questions.answer: It presents one coordinated system covering all species, which points to a single source of command and action.

questions.question: Why is mercy mentioned along with power?
questions.answer: Because the passage is not only about bringing things into existence, but also about caring for them and supplying what they need.

questions.question: If a student had to summarize the reasoning in one sentence, what would be a strong summary?
questions.answer: The ordered revival and care of hundreds of thousands of life forms each spring shows the work of one wise, powerful, and merciful Lord.

questions.question: What season is the focus of the passage, and why is it important?
questions.answer: Spring is the focus because it displays widespread renewal of life that points to resurrection.

questions.question: What number of life forms is highlighted in the passage’s description of the great living host?
questions.answer: Four hundred thousand different species are highlighted.

questions.question: How many revival-like instances are said to be seen in one tree?
questions.answer: Four.

questions.question: What does the repeated return of spring reveal about the way the world is governed?
questions.answer: It reveals stable, intentional, and wise governance.
